get.description:
This API retrieves the bank statement income calculator in an Excel format.

---

Visit our [guide](https://docs.ocrolus.com/docs/bank-statement-income-calculator) for more information.

The output of this endpoint is intended for manual review, as opposed to automated consumption by your application.
> 🚧
> The response will have a MIME type of `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`, hence there is no JSON response schema. See [here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1IeElDLJWQ-YZRmR_zO0OD6ltFnyOPIOQ/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=108945757603422712879&rtpof=true&sd=true) for an example output.

parameters.name: book_uuid
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the <<glossary:Book>> that contains the bank statements you'd like to have analyzed.

get.description:
This API retrieves the Cash Flow Analytics summary of a Book in JSON format. It provides daily balances, bank account PII, and time series for all transaction categories at the <<glossary:Book>> and bank account level. 

It offers quicker analytics generation, more granular and accurate transaction categories (including improved revenue and expense calculations), and a more concise structure.

---

### Async processing 

This API supports asynchronous processing. To get the asynchronous result, add `async=true` in the query parameter to run the request as a background job and receive a `job_id` immediately instead of waiting for the full response inline. When `async=true`, the endpoint returns `202 Accepted` with a `job_id` instead of the analytics payload.

Async mode is required for Books with more than 100,000 transactions. Books exceeding 1,000,000 transactions are rejected with `422` (error code `1100`). Once submitted, poll
[Async job status](https://docs.ocrolus.com/reference/async-job-status) API to retrieve the result when the job is complete.

parameters.name: book_uuid
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the <<glossary:Book>> that contains the bank statements you'd like to have analyzed.

parameters.name: exclude_bank_account_pks
parameters.description:
Bank account primary key(s) to exclude from analytics calculations in the book summary. The underlying data remains in the system and is not deleted.
> 📘 This parameter is in beta. If you encounter any bug, please reach out to [support@ocrolus.com](mailto:support@ocrolus.com).

parameters.name: exclude_months
parameters.description:
Months (in YYYY-MM format) of transaction to exclude from analytics calculations in the book summary. The underlying data remains in the system and is not deleted.
> 📘 This parameter is in beta. If you encounter any bug, please reach out to [support@ocrolus.com](mailto:support@ocrolus.com).

job_id.description: The unique identifier of the async job. Use this value to poll [Async job status](https://docs.ocrolus.com/reference/async-job-status) API for the result.

status.description: The current state of the async job. At submission, this is always `PENDING`. Poll the job status endpoint until the status reaches a terminal state — `DONE` or `FAILED`.
A numerical code that indicates the status of the request.

code.description: A numerical code that indicates the nature of an error.

message.description: A textual description that indicates details about this response's status.

get.description:
This API retrieves pre-engineered analytics on a series of bank statements within a <<glossary:Book>> with an object structure that’s suitable for modeling applications.
> 📘 Note 
  > ***Min_days_to_include**: Minimum number of days required for the most recent calendar month to be included in monthly cash flow calculations. The default value is `0`. If the value is set to **32**, only fully completed months are included.

---
### Async processing 
This API supports asynchronous processing. To get the asynchronous result, add `async=true` in the query parameter to run the request as a background job and receive a `job_id` immediately instead of waiting for the full response inline. When `async=true`, the endpoint returns `202 Accepted` with a `job_id` instead of the analytics payload.
  
Async mode is required for Books with more than 100,000 transactions. Books exceeding 1,000,000 transactions are rejected with `422` (error code `1100`). Once submitted, poll [Async job status](https://docs.ocrolus.com/reference/async-job-status) API to retrieve the result when the job is complete.

parameters.name: book_uuid
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the <<glossary:Book>> that you'd like to analyze. All bank statements in this Book will be analyzed, and other documents will be ignored.

get.description:
This API provides categorizations for each transaction in the requested <<glossary:Book>>. It's the building block for all the Cash Flow Analytics products. It contains a comprehensive list of categories, accurate Transaction tagging, and improved revenue, expense, and transfer logic.

---

### Async processing 

This API supports asynchronous processing. To get the asynchronous result, add `async=true` in the query parameter to run the request as a background job and receive a `job_id` immediately instead of waiting for the full response inline. When `async=true`, the endpoint returns `202 Accepted` with a `job_id` instead of the analytics payload.

Async mode is required for Books with more than 100,000 transactions. Books exceeding 1,000,000 transactions are rejected with `422` (error code `1100`). Once submitted, poll
[Async job status](https://docs.ocrolus.com/reference/async-job-status) API to retrieve the result when the job is complete.

parameters.name: book_uuid
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the <<glossary:Book>> that you'd like to analyze.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: The starting point (number of records to skip) from the latest transaction to fetch results.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of records to be fetched starting from the specified `offset` value.

parameters.name: include_pending_plaid_transactions
parameters.description:
Provides an option to include pending transactions in the response. When set to `true`, the response payload includes an additional `pending_plaid_transactions` field listing currently pending transactions for the Book’s Plaid-linked accounts.

Pending Plaid transactions are transactions that the financial institution has reported to Plaid but which have not yet posted to the account. For example, card authorizations that have not cleared, or ACH debits still in flight. Including them gives you early visibility into recent activity that will eventually appear in the posted transaction set.

> 📘 Note 
> - Pending transactions are surfaced for visibility only. They are not processed through Ocrolus’s enrichment pipeline and therefore do not include tags, categories, or counterparties.
> - These transactions are excluded from all analytics outputs. Cash flow features, Book summaries, risk scores, lender analytics, and analytics exports are computed only from posted transactions.  
> - Once a pending transaction posts at the financial institution, it is processed through enrichment and appears in the standard posted transaction set on the next refresh. The pending entry is then removed.

---

The output of this endpoint is intended for manual review, as opposed to automated consumption by your application.

> 🚧

---

### Async processing

When `async=true`, the endpoint returns `202 Accepted` with a `job_id` instead of the analytics payload.
  
Async mode is required for Books with more than 100,000 transactions. Books exceeding 1,000,000 transactions are rejected with `422` (error code `1100`). Once submitted, poll
[Async job status](https://docs.ocrolus.com/reference/async-job-status) API to retrieve the result when the job is complete.

get.description:
This API retrieves the Risk Score of a Book in JSON format. The Ocrolus Risk Score offers a highly analytical approach to predicting the probability of default for borrowers based on cash flow analytics. This endpoint offers the following benefits:

- Make quicker, more accurate lending decisions backed by data - Leverage alternative data effectively to gain a complete view of borrowers and speed up decision making

- Mitigate credit risk - Easily identifying borrowers that are likely to default with the necessary level of context to understand contributors and detractors

- Expand access to credit and approve more loans for borrowers - Having insight into borrowers’ finances and associated risk can help you see opportunities where others only see risk

### Async processing 

This API supports asynchronous processing. To get the asynchronous result, add `async=true` in the query parameter to run the request as a background job and receive a `job_id` immediately instead of waiting for the full response inline. When `async=true`, the endpoint returns `202 Accepted` with a `job_id` instead of the analytics payload.
    
Async mode is required for Books with more than 100,000 transactions. Books exceeding 1,000,000 transactions are rejected with `422` (error code `1100`). Once submitted, poll
[Async job status](https://docs.ocrolus.com/reference/async-job-status) API to retrieve the result when the job is complete.

parameters.name: book_uuid
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the <<glossary:Book>> that you'd like to analyze.

proba_default.description: The probability of default as a number between 0 and 1, which depicts the likelihood a borrower might default on the loan.

feature_importance.description: A feature vector that depicts the top 10 features that contributed most significantly toward the risk score and the factor by which they contributed. The top features that are returned are specific to each book.

model_version.description: A string representation of the model used to generate prediction.

error.description: A potential error received from the request.

get.description:
Retrieve benchmarking percentiles for an SMB <<glossary:Book>>. The endpoint ranks the Book against anonymized peers across four metrics: revenue, expenses, fintech inflows, and fintech outflows. Use optional query parameters to shape the peer group by time window, geography, and industry granularity.

> 🚧 Early access!
> This feature is available through early access. To enable either feature for your organization, contact your Account Manager.

> 📘 Peer-group validity
> Results are returned only when the peer group contains 30 or more Books. Opted-out organizations are excluded before computation. The same inputs return identical results across the API and the Dashboard.

parameters.name: book_uuid
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the <<glossary:Book>>.

parameters.name: time_window_days
parameters.description: Rolling window, in days, measured back from the Book's creation date. Sets the period over which the Book's metrics and the peer distribution are computed.

parameters.name: geography_type
parameters.description: Geographic scope of the peer group. `msa` uses metropolitan statistical area codes.

parameters.name: geography_code
parameters.description: Geographic identifier for the peer group: a state abbreviation (e.g., `NY`), an MSA code, or `ALL`. Must not be `ALL` when `geography_type` is `state` or `msa`.

parameters.name: industry_level
parameters.description: <<glossary:NAICS>> granularity used to build the peer group.

parameters.name: industry_code
parameters.description: NAICS code matching `industry_level`. Required as a 6-digit code when `industry_level` is `naics6`. Otherwise derived from the Book's NAICS data.

book_uuid.description: The Book for which benchmarking ran.

book_created_ts.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the Book's creation. The `time_window_days` window is measured back from this point.

dimensions.description: The peer-group dimensions the endpoint resolved for this request.

time_window_days.description: The time window applied, in days.

geography_type.description: Geographic scope of the peer group.

geography_code.description: The resolved geography code, or `ALL` for national.

industry_level.description: NAICS granularity used to build the peer group.

industry_code.description: The NAICS code used for the peer group.

value.description: The Book's actual value for that metric over the window.

percentile.description: The Book's percentile rank (0–100) within the peer group, returned as a decimal (e.g., `75.8`).

400.description: Invalid request. Returned for an invalid `book_uuid`, invalid parameter value or combination, or a peer group fewer than 30 books.

status.description: A numerical code that indicates the status of the request.

message.description: A human-readable message providing details about the response status.

code.description: A numerical code that indicates the nature of an error. To learn more about error codes, see [here](https://docs.ocrolus.com/reference/ocrolus-status-codes-api).

get.description: This API retrieve credit shopping events (CSE) for an SMB <<glossary:Book>>. It groups a merchant's loan inquiries into clusters to give lenders visibility into how frequently and how recently the merchant has shopped for credit. The response includes two velocity views — individual loan inquiries and grouped credit-shopping events, along with the full list of events and their anonymized lender inquiry timestamps.

parameters.name: book_uuid
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the <<glossary:Book>>.

business_id.description: The unique identifier of the SMB entity resolved from the Book.

business_name.description: The name of the SMB entity.

loan_inquiry_velocity.description: Count of individual loan inquiries attributed to the SMB within each rolling window, measured back from today.

day_count_30.description: Number of loan inquiries in the last 30 days.

day_count_60.description: Number of loan inquiries in the last 60 days.

day_count_90.description: Number of loan inquiries in the last 90 days.

day_count_180.description: Number of loan inquiries in the last 180 days.

day_count_270.description: Number of loan inquiries in the last 270 days.

day_count_365.description: Number of loan inquiries in the last 365 days.

credit_shopping_velocity.description: Count of Credit Shopping Events (grouped inquiry clusters) within each rolling window. A single event may contain multiple individual inquiries, so these counts will always be less than or equal to the corresponding `loan_inquiry_velocity` counts.

day_count_30.description: Number of Credit Shopping Events in the last 30 days.

day_count_60.description: Number of Credit Shopping Events in the last 60 days.

day_count_90.description: Number of Credit Shopping Events in the last 90 days.

day_count_180.description: Number of Credit Shopping Events in the last 180 days.

day_count_270.description: Number of Credit Shopping Events in the last 270 days.

day_count_365.description: Number of Credit Shopping Events in the last 365 days.

credit_shopping_events.description: One object per Credit Shopping Event, ordered by `first_inquiry_ts`. Each event represents a cluster of loan inquiries grouped by proximity in time. Events are bucketed by the first application date in the chain.

first_inquiry_ts.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the first inquiry in the event. Marks the start of the credit-shopping chain.

last_inquiry_ts.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the last inquiry in the event. Equal to first_inquiry_ts when the event contains a single inquiry (duration_days: 0).

duration_days.description: Span of the event in days, calculated as the difference between first_inquiry_ts and last_inquiry_ts. Returns 0 when all inquiries occurred on the same day.

inquiry_count.description: Total number of loan inquiries in the event across all lenders.

unique_lender_count.description: Number of distinct lenders (organizations) that appear in the event.

lenders.description: One entry per distinct, anonymized lender in the event. Lender identities are not exposed; only their inquiry timestamps are returned.

application_history.description: ISO 8601 timestamps of each inquiry made by this lender within the event, in chronological order.

get.description:
Retrieves the status and result of an analytics job created when any supported analytics endpoint is called with **`async=true`**. Poll this endpoint until the job reaches a terminal state (`DONE` or `FAILED`).

The job **`status`** moves through the following states: **`PENDING`** while the job is running, **`DONE`** when the result is ready, and **`FAILED`** if the job could not be completed. Poll every few seconds until a terminal state is reached. Large Books may take longer to process.

When the status is **`DONE`**, the response includes a **`result_url`**, a temporary pre-signed download link to retrieve the analytics payload, which is identical in shape to the corresponding synchronous endpoint's response. The job and its **`result_url`** are valid for 24 hours from the time the job was created.

parameters.name: job_id
parameters.description: The job ID returned in the `202` response when the async request was submitted.

200.description: The job is complete. Fetch the `result_url` to download the analytics payload. The URL expires 24 hours after the job was created.

job_id.description: The unique identifier of the async job.

status.description: The job completed successfully.

result_url.description: A temporary pre-signed link to download the analytics payload. Expires 24 hours after the job was created.

202.description: The job is still running. Keep polling until the status changes to `DONE` or `FAILED`.

job_id.description: The unique identifier of the async job.

status.description: The job is in progress. Poll again after a few seconds.

404.description: The job ID is not recognized, does not belong to your organization, or has expired. Jobs expire 24 hours after creation.

job_id.description: The job ID that was not found.

error.description: A description of why the job ID could not be found.

422.description: The job failed. The `error` field explains why. For example, a book that exceeds 1,000,000 transactions is rejected with `422`.

job_id.description: The unique identifier of the async job.

status.description: The job failed.

error.description: A description of why the job failed.
error.example: Book transaction count exceeds the maximum supported by the async serving path

alt_lender_payments_by_month.title: Alternative Lender Payments by Month
alt_lender_payments_by_month.description: Debits (i.e. payments) made to alternative lenders grouped by calendar month. Provides context into a customer's access to competitive financing as well as debt service requirements. Each key is a string representing a month and a year, using the regex `^\d{2}/\d{4}$` (i.e `MM/YYYY`).

average_by_month.title: Average Transaction Size by Month
average_by_month.description: The average absolute value of all transactions grouped by calendar month. Each key is a string representing a month and a year, using the regex `^\d{2}/\d{4}$` (i.e `MM/YYYY`).

average_daily_balance.title: Average Daily Balance
average_daily_balance.description: The average daily ending balance (including weekends).

average_daily_balance_by_month.title: Average Daily Balance by Month
average_daily_balance_by_month.description: The average daily ending balance (including weekends) grouped by calendar month. Each key is a string representing a month and a year, using the regex `^\d{2}/\d{4}$` (i.e `MM/YYYY`).

average_daily_balance_weekday.title: Average Daily Balance (Weekdays)
average_daily_balance_weekday.description: The average daily ending balance of weekdays.

average_daily_balance_weekday_by_month.title: Average Daily Balance (Weekdays) by Month
average_daily_balance_weekday_by_month.description: The average daily ending balance of weekdays grouped by calendar month. Each key is a string representing a month and a year, using the regex `^\d{2}/\d{4}$` (i.e `MM/YYYY`).

average_deposit_by_month.title: Average Deposit by Month
average_deposit_by_month.description: The average value of credit transactions grouped by calendar month. Each key is a string representing a month and a year, using the regex `^\d{2}/\d{4}$` (i.e `MM/YYYY`).

bank_accounts.title: Bank Account Level Analytics
bank_accounts.description: List of Bank Account Level JSONs

cash_expense_days_by_month.title: Cash Expense Days by Month
cash_expense_days_by_month.description: Cash expense days grouped by month. Measures the amount of runway a business has given its operating expenses. Cash expense days = (average daily balance)/(average daily expense) Each key is a string representing a month and a year, using the regex `^\d{2}/\d{4}$` (i.e `MM/YYYY`).

daily_balances.title: Running Daily Balance
daily_balances.description: A list of the daily ending balances for every day. Each key is a string representing a date, using the regex `^\d{2}/\d{2}/\d{4}$` (i.e `MM/DD/YYYY`).

daily_balances_by_month.title: Running Daily Balance by Month
daily_balances_by_month.description: A list of the daily ending balances for every day grouped by month.

daily_balances_weekday.title: Running Daily Balance Weekday
daily_balances_weekday.description: A list of the daily ending balances for every weekday. Each key is a string representing a date, using the regex `^\d{2}/\d{2}/\d{4}$` (i.e `MM/DD/YYYY`).

daily_balances_weekday_by_month.title: Running Daily Balance Weekday by Month
daily_balances_weekday_by_month.description:
A list of the daily ending balances for every weekday grouped by month.
Each key is a string representing a month and a year, using the regex `^\d{2}/\d{4}$` (i.e `MM/YYYY`).
Each value is an object with keys that are string representations of a date, using the regex `^\d{2}/\d{2}/\d{4}$` (i.e `MM/DD/YYYY`).

deposit_count.title: Deposit Count
deposit_count.description: The total number of credit transactions.

estimated_daily_expense_by_month.title: Estimated Daily Expense by Month
estimated_daily_expense_by_month.description: Estimated daily expenses grouped by month. Important for understanding the costs required to operate the business as well as the firm's ability to adapt spending during a period of disruption. Each key is a string representing a month and a year, using the regex `^\d{2}/\d{4}$` (i.e `MM/YYYY`).

estimated_expense_by_month.title: Estimated Expense by Month
estimated_expense_by_month.description: Estimated monthly expenses grouped by calendar month. Important for understanding the costs required to operate the business as well as the firm's ability to adapt spending during a period of disruption. Each key is a string representing a month and a year, using the regex `^\d{2}/\d{4}$` (i.e `MM/YYYY`).

estimated_revenue_by_month.title: Estimated Revenue by Month
estimated_revenue_by_month.description:
The estimated revenue of the business grouped by calendar month. This is calculated by summing together all credit transactions, then removing all transfer credits (except for wire transfers), all alternative lender credits (except for factoring credits), and all transactions that contain words that signify that they are not revenue deposits. This includes words such as "Refund", "Reversal", "Cash Back", "Return", and about 20 others.
Each key is a string representing a month and a year, using the regex `^\d{2}/\d{4}$` (i.e `MM/YYYY`).

mca_payments_by_month.title: MCA Payments by Month
mca_payments_by_month.description: Debits (i.e. payments) made to merchant cash advance lenders, broken out by month. Provides context into a customer's access to competitive financing as well as debt service requirements. Each key is a string representing a month and a year, using the regex `^\d{2}/\d{4}$` (i.e `MM/YYYY`).

name.title: Name
name.description: Name of the Book or bank account

negative_balances_by_month.title: List of Days Negative Balance by Month
negative_balances_by_month.description: The list of all days in which the daily ending balance fell below zero grouped by calendar month. Each key is a string representing a month and a year, using the regex `^\d{2}/\d{4}$` (i.e `MM/YYYY`). Months with no days ending with a negative balance are represented with empty arrays.

negative_balances_by_month_weekday.title: List of Weekdays with Negative Balance by Month
negative_balances_by_month_weekday.description: The list of all weekdays in which the daily ending balance fell below zero grouped by calendar month. Each key is a string representing a month and a year, using the regex `^\d{2}/\d{4}$` (i.e `MM/YYYY`). Months with no days ending with a negative balance are represented with empty arrays.

BankAccountAnalytics.description: Detailed analytics computed on a particular bank account. A <<glossary:Book>> may contain bank statements from multiple bank accounts, therefore the Book analytics may contain multiple objects of this type.

account_category.title: Bank Account Category
account_category.description: Indicates different categories of bank accounts captured from documents.

account_holder.title: Bank Account Holder
account_holder.description: The name of the person or entity who owns this bank account.

account_holders.title: Bank Account Holders
account_holders.description: This field will be a single-element array with the value given in `account_holder`.

account_number.title: Bank Account Number
account_number.description: The captured number of this bank account.

account_type.title: Bank Account Type
account_type.description: Bank account type indicates the different types of bank accounts captured from documents.

alt_lender_payments_by_month.description: Debits (i.e. payments) made to alternative lenders grouped by calendar month. Provides context into a customer's access to competitive financing as well as debt service requirements. Each key is a string representing a month and a year, using the regex `^\d{2}/\d{4}$` (i.e `MM/YYYY`).

alternative_lender_transactions.title: List of Alternative Lender Transactions
alternative_lender_transactions.description: A list of all transactions to/from alternative lenders, including small business lenders, personal lenders, and mortgage players. This list also includes transactions relating to Merchant Cash Advance and Factoring, though these are separately filtered in unique lists for Merchant Cash Advance Transactions and Factoring Transactions.

atm_withdrawals_num.title: Number of ATM Withdrawals

atm_withdrawals_sum.title: Amount of ATM Withdrawals
atm_withdrawals_sum.description: The sum of all atm withdrawal amounts

average_alt_lender_payments.title: Average Monthly Alternative Lender Payments
average_alt_lender_payments.description: Average monthly debits (i.e. payments) made to alternative lenders. Provides context into a customer's access to competitive financing as well as debt service requirements.

average_daily_balance.title: Average Daily Balance
average_daily_balance.description: The average daily ending balance (including weekends).

average_daily_balance_by_month.title: Average Daily Balance by Month
average_daily_balance_by_month.description: The average daily ending balance (including weekends) grouped by calendar month. Each key is a string representing a month and a year, using the regex `^\d{2}/\d{4}$` (i.e `MM/YYYY`).

average_daily_balance_weekday.title: Average Daily Balance (Weekdays)
average_daily_balance_weekday.description: The average daily ending balance of weekdays.

average_daily_balance_weekday_by_month.title: Average Daily Balance (Weekdays) by Month

Transaction.description: Detailed information about a specific credit or debit within a bank account.

page_idx.description: The page number of the original document from which this transaction was captured.

bank_account_pk.description: The primary key of the bank account from which this transaction was captured.

amount.description: The amount of the credit or debit that this transaction represents. Will be in USD, and can be positive or negative.

bbox.description:
The coordinates of the bounding box (i.e. rectangle) on the page from which this transaction was captured.
Unit of measurement is in pixels, and the origin (`[0, 0]`) is in the top-left corner.
The bounding box is encoded as `[x, y, x+w, y+h]`, where:

- `x` is the horizontal position of the box, relative to the left of the page.
- `y` is the vertical position of the bounding box, relative to the top of the page.
- `w` is the width of the bounding box.
- `h` is the height of the bounding box.

txn_date.description: The date on which this transaction occurred. Given in `MM/DD/YYYY` format.

page_doc_pk.description: The unique identifier of the page from which this transaction was captured.

pk.description: The unique identifier of this particular transaction.

uploaded_doc_pk.description: The unique identifier of the document from which this transaction was captured.

description.description: Details about the transaction that were captured from the original bank statement.

deducted_transfer_deposit_txns.description: Credit transactions identified as transfers. Deducted from the total revenue estimate.

EstimatedRevenueCalculationTransactionsB.title: Estimated Revenue Calculation Transactions by Month
EstimatedRevenueCalculationTransactionsB.description:
The list of credit transactions used to calculate estimated revenues grouped by category and calendar month.
estimated_revenue = all credits - revenue_deducted -  transfer + revenue_included - alternative_lender + factoring The estimated revenue of the business grouped by calendar month. This is calculated by summing together all credit transactions, then removing all transfer credits (except for wire transfers), all alternative lender credits (except for factoring credits), and all transactions that contain words that signify that they are not revenue deposits. This includes words such as "Refund", "Reversal", "Cash Back", "Return", and about 20 others.

added_factoring_txns.description:
Credit transactions identified as factoring. Added to the total revenue estimate.
Each key is a string representing a month and a year, using the regex `^\d{2}/\d{4}$` (i.e `MM/YYYY`).

Each key is a string representing a month and a year, using the regex `^\d{2}/\d{4}$` (i.e `MM/YYYY`).

deposits.description:

deducted_specific_terms_txns.description:

Each key is a string representing a month and a year, using the regex `^\d{2}/\d{4}$` (i.e `MM/YYYY`).

AnalyticsRequestStatus.description:
The current state of the asynchronous analytics request.
The possible values are defined as follows:

- **`COMPLETED`:** The request has completed and the resulting analytics object is enclosed.
- **`PROCESSING`:** The request is still being processed.
Check back later.
- **`EXPIRED`:** The request has been processed,
and the window of time to retrieve the results has passed.
If you still need the data returned by this request, submit a new one.

naics_description.description:
The description of the 4-digit NAICS code, indicating the industry classification of the Book category.

  > 📘 In Books with multiple businesses or fragmented merchant activity, the widget may show the following statuses as applicable:
  > - **`Pending - Industry Data`**: Classification is in progress.  
  > - **`Unable to find a unique SMB merchant`**: The system is not able to find a unique merchant mapped to the documents in the Book.  
  > - **`Not Available`**: The system has found a unique merchant, but this merchant does not have industry classification data.

sic_code.description: A four-digit Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) code that identifies the merchant’s primary business activity using the legacy SIC system. SIC codes are derived from bank statement data and are used for industry classification, regulatory reporting, and analytics.

periods.description:
A list of statement periods covered by the Book. Each period represents the date range of a single bank statement.

**Reconciliation field behavior**
When `reconciled` is `true`, `recon_error_absolute_amount` is `null` or `0` and all other recon fields are `null`.

When `reconciled` is `false`, `recon_error_absolute_amount` is populated and remaining recon fields are populated where available.

Reconciliation values are consistent with the transactions endpoint.

begin_date.description: The start date of the statement period retrieved from the summary section of a bank statement.

end_date.description: The end date of the statement period retrieved from the summary section of a bank statement.

begin_balance.description: The initial balance of the statement period retrieved from the summary section of a bank statement.

end_balance.description: The final balance of the statement period retrieved from the summary section of a bank statement.

txn_count.description: The count of transactions that were included in the analytics calculation for this particular period.

uploaded_doc_pk.description: The unique identifier of the document from which this transaction is captured.

average_amount.description: The mean absolute amount of transactions within a given statement period.

average_daily_balance.description: The average daily ending balance including weekends.

average_daily_cash_flow.description: The mean daily net cash flow, calculated as the difference between total credits and total debits. The `Net Cash Flow = Credits - Debits`.

average_deposit.description: The average amount of credit transactions.

deposit_sum.description: The overall amount credit during the specified period.

deposit_count.description: The total number of deposit occurrences during the specified period.

withdrawal_sum.description: The overall amount withdrawn during the specified period.

withdrawal_count.description: The total count of withdrawals during the specified period.

negative_balances_weekday.description: Days in which the daily ending balance fell below zero.

nsf_fee_sum.description: The sum of all NSF fee amounts in the statement period.

nsf_fee_count.description: The number of NSF occurrences in the statement period.

nsf_raw_fee_count.description: The total NSF fee count (NOT including common divisor logic) in statement period.

overdraft_fee_sum.description: The sum of all overdraft fee amounts in the statement period.

overdraft_fee_count.description: The number of overdraft occurrences in the statement period.

overdraft_raw_fee_count.description: The total overdraft fee count (NOT including common divisor logic) in statement period.

returned_item_deposit_count.description: The total number of returned item credits.

returned_item_withdrawal_count.description: The total number of returned item debits.

has_weekend_txn.description: Indicates if any transactions occured on a weekend.

nsf_divisor.description: The calculated amount for a single NSF fee.

overdraft_divisor.description: The calculated amount for a single overdraft fee.

max_deposit.description: The highest single deposit amount recorded during the period.

average_withdrawal.description: The average withdrawal amount across all withdrawals during the period. Returned as a negative value.

max_withdrawal.description: The largest single withdrawal amount recorded during the period. Returned as a negative value.

revenue_count.description: The total number of transactions tagged as revenue during the period.

revenue_deduction.description: The total amount deducted from gross revenue during the period based on the active revenue formula.

expense.description: The total amount of transactions tagged as expenses during the period. Returned as a negative value.

expense_count.description: The total number of transactions tagged as expenses during the period.

negative_balances.description: A list of dates within the period on which the account balance was negative. Returns an empty array if no negative balances were recorded.

nsf_days_count.description: The number of days within the period on which a non-sufficient funds (NSF) event was recorded.

overdraft_days_count.description: The number of days within the period on which an overdraft event was recorded.

nsf_or_overdraft_days_count.description: The total number of days within the period on which either an NSF or overdraft event was recorded.

large_deposits.description: The total amount of deposits considered large during the period, based on Ocrolus thresholds.

reconciled.description: Whether the statement period reconciled successfully. `true` means the opening and closing balances match the transactions, and `false` means a discrepancy was detected.

recon_error_absolute_amount.description: The dollar amount of the reconciliation discrepancy for the period. Returns null or 0 when the period reconciled or returns the discrepancy amount when it did not.

recon_error_pct_of_average_daily_balance.description: The reconciliation discrepancy expressed as a percentage of the average daily balance. Helps you identify the relative size of the error. Returns null when the period reconciled or when average daily balance is unavailable.

primary_recon_error_reason.description: The main reason the period did not reconcile, such as a balance mismatch or missing transactions. Returns null when the period reconciled.

secondary_recon_error_reason.description: An additional reason contributing to the reconciliation failure, where available. Returns null when the period reconciled or when no secondary reason is identified.

high_amount_average_daily_balance.description: Returns `true` if the average daily balance for this period is unusually high compared to typical activity. May indicate large deposits or infrequent withdrawals.

balance_ending_with_zero.description: Returns `true` if the account balance reached zero at the end of this period. May indicate the account was fully drawn down.

high_txns_count_atm_over_cash.description: Returns `true` if the number of ATM transactions is disproportionately high relative to cash transactions during this period.

has_weekend_transactions.description: Returns `true` if any transactions occurred on weekends during this period. Useful for identifying business type and activity patterns.

no_txn_in_weekdays_within_period.description: Returns `true` if no transactions were recorded on weekdays during this period. May indicate account inactivity or an unusual cash flow pattern.

high_txns_amount_atm_over_cash.description: Returns `true` if the total amount of ATM transactions is disproportionately high relative to cash transactions during this period.
